A.note: Flat, evenly lit and washed out. Smooth water has little sparkle. The ships are slab hulls with floating flat sail cards, like game pieces. The town reads at a distance but has no people, smoke or life. Fortification walls are plain extruded boxes.

B.note: Same geometry as A, with more saturated colour and a livelier water surface with foam highlights. The ships are still toy-like, with no rigging, no wake and no crew. The water is a bit oversaturated and cartoonish, but it adds energy.

C.note: Same geometry as B, with the best grading. Warm sunlight, stronger terrain shadows and contrast, and better material separation on the roofs and walls. It reads as a more cinematic golden-hour scene. The ships remain the weakest element: dark slab hulls with floating sail cards. Still no life in the harbour.

why: The geometry is identical in all three, so the ranking comes down to lighting and grading. C has the warmest, most directional light and the best depth. B has livelier water. A is flat and washed out.
top_fix_for_best: Rebuild the three ships with proper hull curvature, gunports, rigging, billowing sails and bow wakes. Then add harbour life: small boats, smoke from chimneys and batteries, and a few flags. The ships are the toy-like element that most undermines the otherwise convincing town.
